title: Israel's new Knesset elects an Eisenkot ally as speaker, a defeat for Netanyahu's bloc
seoTitle: Knesset speaker vote: Kahana elected, a blow to Netanyahu
dek: Matan Kahana of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party won 66 votes to 52 on 17 November, with backing from Arab-majority parties, replacing Netanyahu ally Amir Ohana. No government has been formed since the 27 October election.
happened: In Israel's 27 October election neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot won a majority: Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats, Eisenkot's bloc 48, and two Arab-majority slates (Ra'am and the Joint List) an unprecedented 19. On 17 November the new Knesset elected Yashar's Matan Kahana as speaker by 66 votes to 52 over Likud's Ofir Katz, after a filibuster by the Netanyahu bloc that lasted six to seven hours. The Arab parties backed Kahana. He replaces Likud's Amir Ohana, speaker since 2022. Netanyahu's and Eisenkot's parties met on 15 November to discuss a possible unity government; Al Jazeera reports both men say they should be prime minister.

sides.says: "I will be a Knesset speaker for everyone, irrespective of race, religion or gender." He said the Knesset "will unquestioningly obey the court's rulings" while he is speaker.

"The Knesset will return to being the house of the people, of all the people." He says he wants to rescind the reforms that reduced judicial independence and to set up a state commission of inquiry into the security failures before Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack.

Likud said Kahana was "unilaterally appointed with the votes of terror supporters" and called the vote "a low point in the Knesset's history". Bezalel Smotrich called it an "eternal disgrace" and Itamar Ben Gvir wrote "Shame". Netanyahu has refused an independent inquiry into 7 October. He is not quoted directly in the reports read here.

next: Coalition talks continue, including on a possible unity government. The Times of Israel, citing Ynet, reports that Eisenkot's bloc agreed not to advance repeal of the judicial overhaul laws until Monday, 23 November, in return for the Netanyahu bloc ending its filibuster.
summary: Israel's new parliament elected Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, as speaker on 17 November by 66 votes to 52, with Arab-majority parties' support, replacing a Netanyahu ally. Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority in the 27 October election (53 seats to the Eisenkot bloc's 48, with 19 for Arab-majority parties), and no government has yet been formed. Eisenkot wants to undo the judicial overhaul and set up a state inquiry into 7 October; Likud called the vote a low point in the Knesset's history.
